podcast.title: Almost Signed Aretha Franklin
podcast.body: Blue Note Records was very close to signing Aretha Franklin. Plans were made for a recording project in Detroit centered around her piano playing, with Jerry Jemmott and Bernard Purdie, but it was thwarted by Aretha's illness. "We came this close to having her sign to Blu-Nob Really? Yeah, and I went to Detroit a couple times I'd known her And I said she got to play piano."

podcast.title: Founding and Legacy
podcast.body: Blue Note Records is described as "one of the first and longest standing institutions of jazz music," founded in 1939. It is celebrating its 85th anniversary in 2024. The label is known for its "cooler branding," attributed to art director Reed Miles and photographer-turned-executive Francis Wolfe. Over its history, it has released albums by numerous prominent artists including Herbie Hancock, Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, Robert Glasper, Lee Morgan, John Coltrane, Wayne Shorter, Bobby McFerrin, Greg Porter, Ron Carter, Michelle Andegeo Cello, Charles Lloyd, and Julian Lodge. "Blue Note is one of the first and longest standing institutions of jazz music."

podcast.title: Presidency and Vision
podcast.body: Don Was is the current president of Blue Note Records, leading the label's 85th-anniversary celebrations in 2024. He expressed his intention to speak with artists representing the label's past, present, and future, including Ron Carter, Michelle Andegeo Cello, Charles Lloyd, Julian Lodge, and Nora Jones. "Blue Note's current president, Don Was, to speak with the label's past, present, and future."

podcast.title: Signing Nora Jones
podcast.body: Bruce Lentval, the head of Blue Note Records at the time, met Nora Jones after an EMI publishing contact set up a meeting. Nora presented a three-song demo, and despite Lentval remarking that some of it "isn't jazz... This is country," he decided to sign her, stating, "I don't care. Let's do it. Let's make a record." This decision allowed Nora to embark on her entire career with the label. "Bruce listened and he liked it. And then after the Jesse song came on, he goes, well, what do you want to be a jazz singer or a pop singer? I was like, jazz singer. I'm here in Boone Records, Jesse. Correct answer, right? Yeah."

podcast.title: Sister Label Manhattan Records
podcast.body: Manhattan Records, a label focused on classical, musical theater, and adult contemporary, was considered a sister label to Blue Note and was overseen by Bruce Lundvall. "Manhattan Records, which was a sort of sister label to Blue Note that Bruce oversaw, which was either classical or musical theater kind of adult contemporary."
